case_name: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited v R. Santhakumari Velusamy and others
facts: The appellant, Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd., is the successor of the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, and Government of India (for short 'government' or 'telecom department').
There were four grades of employees of telecom departments known as Telegraphists or Telecom Operating Assistants in the Telecom Department.
The government decided that a second time bound promotion was not feasible.

Under the said scheme, employees who were in regular service as on 1.1.1990 and had completed 26 years of satisfactory service in the basic cadres, were to be screened by a duly constituted Committee to assess their performance and determine their suitability for advancement and if they were found suitable, to be upgraded in the higher scale.
The upgradation was restricted to 10% of the posts in Grade III.
By letter dated 7.5.1993, the telecom department clarified that there were no sanctioned posts in regard to 10% BCR and the number of posts depend upon the number of BCR officials available;

The government issued an order dated 8.9.1999 directing that a Review DPC be held and all ineligible officers wrongly promoted to Grade IV by application of reservation roster as per office order dated 1.3.1996, should be reverted back and all eligible officers should be placed in Grade IV and their pay should be fixed notionally.
Feeling aggrieved, the contesting respondents filed applications before the Madras Bench of the Tribunal.
A Full Bench of the Tribunal at Bangalore allowed the applications by order dated 26.4.2000.

The Full Bench of the Tribunal differed from the decision of its Ahmadabad Bench and held that the decision of the Gujarat High Court affirming the said decision was also of no assistance as it was at variance with the decisions of this Court in Union of India vs. S.S. Ranade - 1995 (4) SCC 462 1995 Indlaw SC 1056, Lalit Mohan Deb v. Union of India - 1973 (3) SCC 862 1972 Indlaw SC 632, State of Rajasthan vs. Fateh Chand Soni - 1996 (1) SCC 562 1995 Indlaw SC 1901, and Ram Prasad vs. D.K. Vijay - 1999 (7) SCC 251 1999 Indlaw SC 724.

Following the said decision of the Full Bench of the Tribunal, the Madras Bench of the Tribunal by order dated 25.7.2000 allowed the applications filed by the contesting respondents herein and directed the government to restore the contesting respondents to their promoted posts which they were holding before the order dated 8.9.1999.
issues: What is the nature of upgradation under the Biennial Cadre Review (BCR) scheme?
Do the rules of reservation apply to promotions in Grade IV under the BCR scheme?
Can a distinction be drawn between upgradation and promotion based on the nomenclature only?
petitioner_arguments: The government argued that the decision of the Gujarat High Court affirming the said decision was also of no assistance as it was at variance with the decisions of this Court in Union of India vs. S.S. Ranade - 1995 (4) SCC 462 1995 Indlaw SC 1056, Lalit Mohan Deb v. Union of India - 1973 (3) SCC 862 1972 Indlaw SC 632, State of Rajasthan vs. Fateh Chand Soni - 1996 (1) SCC 562 1995 Indlaw SC 1901, and Ram Prasad vs. D.K. Vijay - 1999 (7) SCC 251 1999 Indlaw SC 724.
The government argued that the BCR upgradation to Grade IV in the telecom department amounted to promotion, attracting reservation for SCs and STs.
respondent_arguments: The contesting respondents argued that principles of reservation would not apply for upgradation of existing posts which did not carry any change in duties and responsibilities.
The contesting respondents argued that appointments to upgraded posts with higher scales of pay were in effect a substitute for promotion.
court_reasoning: The Full Bench of the Tribunal held that the BCR upgradation to Grade IV in the telecom department amounted to promotion, attracting reservation for SCs and STs.

It held that this process can only be treated as promotion in the light of the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that an appointment to a higher scale of pay even at the same post and even without involving any additional responsibilities can still be a promotion.

The Full Bench of the Tribunal differed from the decision of its Ahmadabad Bench and held that the decision of the Gujarat High Court affirming the said decision was also of no assistance as it was at variance with the decisions of this Court in Union of India vs. S.S. Ranade - 1995 (4) SCC 462 1995 Indlaw SC 1056, Lalit Mohan Deb v. Union of India - 1973 (3) SCC 862 1972 Indlaw SC 632, State of Rajasthan vs. Fateh Chand Soni - 1996 (1) SCC 562 1995 Indlaw SC 1901, and Ram Prasad vs. D.K. Vijay - 1999 (7) SCC 251 1999 Indlaw SC 724.
holding: The Full Bench of the Tribunal at Bangalore allowed the applications by order dated 26.4.2000.

The Madras Bench of the Tribunal by order dated 25.7.2000 allowed the applications filed by the contesting respondents herein and directed the government to restore the contesting respondents to their promoted posts which they were holding before the order dated 8.9.1999.
